precepts.text: Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him. That was the guy that put the talent in the napkin; he drew back. As we're doing the restructuring, we'll ask certain captains, hey, why did you move this brother from this position to this position? Oh, he's not the same anymore. When he came in, he was on fire; we didn't have to tell him what to do. Now you got to yell at this guy, you got to force him. So let's drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” That was the guy who put the talent in the napkin: he drew back.

As we're doing the restructuring, certain captains get asked, why did you move this brother from this position to that position? Oh, he's not the same any more. When he came in, he was on fire; we didn't have to tell him what to do. Now you've got to yell at him, you've got to force him. So drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.

The Lord has no pleasure in the one who draws back. That is walking feignedly before him, and Ezra asks God to think not upon those, but to remember them that according to his will have known his fear.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not: God did not want it any more. He taketh away the first covenant of animal sacrifice, that he may establish the second, the new covenant in Christ, by the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. The Pharisees would say it is in the law, you must do animal sacrifice, and they would neglect the scriptures pointing to Christ.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law.” God didn't want it no more. Mark “which are offered by the law”: the law does say to do it, and the Pharisees would use that and say, no, it's in the law, you must do animal sacrifice. They would neglect the descriptions of Christ in Isaiah 53, in Zechariah 9 of the king coming lowly, and in the Psalms.

“Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” He took away the first covenant of animal sacrifice, that he might establish the second covenant, the new covenant in Christ: “By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

So the scribes were ignoring that. They said, we're not dealing with that. But the offering of Christ's body once for all is what blotted out the ordinances and nailed them to his cross.

precepts.text: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. It was temporary.
precepts.point: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Colossians says the meats, drinks, holy days, new moons and sabbaths the people were being judged by “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come. Hebrews says it the same way: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

The law of sacrifice was a shadow of things to come, which was Christ. It was not the very image. Those sacrifices offered year after year could never make the people perfect. It was temporary.

That is why the scribes and Pharisees were beguiling the people when they said, go back to the lamb, go back to the goat. The Sabbath had once been esteemed with two lambs of the first year; Christ came and fulfilled that. The shadow pointed to him, and the body is of Christ.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me. The animal sacrifices were temporary, a shadow training us for what was to come; the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ. Lo, I come in the volume of the book: the whole book, because Christ is present in the Old Testament and before it.
precepts.point: Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. His people; that is who the sacrifice was for.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
To expound further on Christ being the ultimate sacrifice: “Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”. The body was Christ. The sacrificial laws of animal sacrifice were a preparation for what was to come, a shadow of good things to come; the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ, dying only for the nation of Israel.

“In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.” The Most High had no pleasure in those sacrifices. They were temporary, to train us and prepare us for Christ.

“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” In the volume of the book: the whole book, not just the New Testament. Christ is present in the Old Testament, and Christ is present before the Old Testament.

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law”. So the offerings of the law pointed to the body prepared for him, the one sacrifice that saves his people from their sins.

precepts.text: Then said I, Lo, I come in the volume of the book. Christ comes in the volume of the book: it is written of him. When you read the Bible and it says the Lord said this and the Lord did that, it is talking about Christ. He was the one speaking right through the scriptures, dealing with us right through the scriptures.
precepts.point: For my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them: these words are the Lord's spirit.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” The book of the Lord is the Bible, and whose book is it? Hebrews answers: “Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.”

Christ comes in the volume of the book. Everybody has to understand that. The Lord comes in the volume of the book, and it is written of him. When you read the Bible and it says the Lord said this and the Lord did that, it is talking about Christ. He is the one who was speaking right through the scriptures, and he is the one who was dealing with us right through the scriptures.

So tie it back to Isaiah: seek ye out of the book of the Lord, the book of the Lord. What we read there is written of him; that is him, the Lord, right there. And because it is his book and his word, “no one of these shall fail.” Nothing written in it will fail. Everything we read about in it is going to come to pass, whether you believe or not, and you cannot mate the Bible with any other book.

“for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” The words on those pages are the Lord’s spirit, the words of Christ, who came in the volume of the book to do the will of God.

precepts.text: Ye had compassion of me in my bonds and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods: the Israelites who supported Paul lost their homes and properties.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” They did it in the time of Rome, when the Pharisees did it with Rome's guidance. Paul tells the Hebrews, “For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.”

Ye had compassion of me in my bonds: when Paul was in prison, they supported him. And they took joyfully the spoiling, the robbing, of their goods: their homes and houses, lands and properties. Those Israelites sacrificed their whole livelihood. They knew that supporting Paul would reveal them, and whatever they had would be taken.

Are we prepared for that? Do we really think about it? The cushy side of the room: I'm so comfortable, I got my new house, my new car, my new hair, my new nails. Are you ready for what the scriptures say is going to happen? Are we willing to lose everything, knowing we have in heaven a better and enduring substance? That is another level of faith we have to build ourselves up to in the short, limited time we have.

Even the world is warning that if a crisis comes and the government says get on a bus for your safety, do not get on: prepare your food, water, power and shelter so you do not have to rely on them. We have been telling our people that for years.

precepts.text: He that despised Moses' law died without mercy: no grace under Moses, and you are not David, Moses or Esther, so do not try it.
precepts.point: There is now no condemnation to them in Christ Jesus who walk after the Spirit: condemnation is the death you got by stoning, fire or the tree for what no animal could atone. The law of the Spirit of life in Christ has made me free, given me liberty, from the law of sin and death: sin under Moses got you certain death without repentance, and that law was weak through the flesh because the people offering were sinful.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus”. The condemnation goes back to the curse on him that continueth not in all things written in the law. Almost all things were purged with blood, not all. There were sins no animal could help you atone for, and if you fell under that, you got condemnation: death. You got stoned to death, set on fire, or hung from a tree.

That is “the law of sin and death”, the law of sacrifice. Hebrews shows it: “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”. He that hated Moses’ law, the law we all agreed to keep, died without mercy. There was no grace under Moses. If you sinned a certain sin against the Lord, you got immediate death. There was no, I’m sorry, I repent, I didn’t mean to. It was death. Condemnation and death are synonymous.

The Most High had mercy on David, on Moses, on Solomon. But you are not David, you are not Solomon, you are not Moses, you are not Esther. Do not even try that, because you will.

“For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh”: the law of sin and death was weak because the people offering the sacrifices were weak and sinful. “The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death”: made me free, given me liberty. By Christ “all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” Under the animals you could not repent of everything; under Christ’s death you can. That is why there is now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.

precepts.text: He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses. Under Moses there was no grace: sins like breaking the Sabbath, homosexuality, and idolatry had no animal, and refusing to sacrifice at all meant death. You were indebted to continual offerings.
precepts.point: To him that worketh not, that offers no sacrifice, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness, as David describeth the blessedness of the man unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works. The Lord deemed Abraham faithful before he sacrificed animals.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Romans 4:4 says “Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.” To him that offers sacrifices, the reward is not reckoned of grace or mercy, but of debt, because under Moses there was no grace. Hebrews shows it: “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”. Without mercy means without grace.

If you chose to do something worthy of death that an animal could not atone for, you had to die. If you broke the Sabbath, you couldn't atone with an animal. Homosexuality, you couldn't atone with an animal. Idolatry, you couldn't atone with an animal. And if you chose not to sacrifice at all, you had to die. So you were indebted to offer continual sacrifices all the time: continual burnt offerings, drink offerings, sin offerings.

The prophets said the temple would be destroyed. Once the temple is gone, where are your works? If your salvation rests on sacrificing an animal and there is no animal, no priest and no temple to atone with, by default you have condemned yourself. That is why faith in Christ has to supersede the works.

“But to him that worketh not”, him that does not offer sacrifice, “but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.” Christ justifies the ungodly through his death. Just as with Abraham, who was counted faithful before he sacrificed animals, God “imputeth righteousness without works”. Israel could keep sacrificing while the temple stood, but Christ had to come first in their minds, or they were in debt.

precepts.text: The daily sacrifices can never take away sins, but this man offered one sacrifice for sins for ever and sat down on the right hand of God.
precepts.point: The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

precepts.why:
“And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God”. “we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

So the day of atonement is still kept: the tenth day of the seventh month, afflicting the soul and doing no work at all, an everlasting statute. But it is kept without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal. The blood of the sin offering of atonements that Aaron put on the horns of the altar once in a year has been answered by one sacrifice for sins for ever.

precepts.text: The law had a shadow of good things to come; the blood of bulls and goats could never take away sins, so Christ had to be the ultimate sacrifice.
precepts.point: That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
This is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: “the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

If they could have, “would they not have ceased to be offered?” Instead “in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year. For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.” We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice.

Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ’s coming, the shadow of the good thing to come.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; he taketh away the first covenant to establish the second, and this man offered one sacrifice for sins for ever and sat down.
precepts.point: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God. Christ took away the first covenant to establish the second, and we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. Men had been sacrificing since the days of Adam; when Christ came, one sacrifice ended it, because that lamb had no blemish. The law of sacrifice was always temporary, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was Christ.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
The people got redundant with it: “every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins”. They kept sinning and kept bringing sacrifices instead of repenting, thinking it was okay to sin as long as the offerings kept coming. It is the same spirit today, wicked all weekend and a hundred dollars in the plate on Sunday; the Most High does not want your money, He wants you to repent. Only you can put away your sins, when you repent and stop sinning.

“Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” Christ took away the first covenant to establish the second, “By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

“But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God”. Men had been sacrificing since the days of Adam; when Christ came, one sacrifice ended it, because that lamb had no blemish. The law of sacrifice in Leviticus 4 was always temporary, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was Christ.

precepts.text: If we sin wilfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins.
precepts.point: That is the judgment on the willful: if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins. That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. The Lord knoweth all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts; he knoweth your inventions and what ye think in your heart, even them that sin and would hide their sin. Sin willfully and your grace period is up.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
That is the judgment on the willful: “if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins”.

The ruler who sinned through ignorance had a sacrifice, the kid of the goats, and it was forgiven him. The man gathering sticks, who knew the law, had none. Sin willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth and your grace period is up.

precepts.text: Lo, I come in the volume of the book it is written of me; the whole book from Genesis to Revelation points to Christ.
precepts.point: The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” The whole book from Genesis to Revelation points to Christ, and the whole law of sacrifice points to him.

The ram without blemish, perfect as the Most High made it, is the offering without blemish that Christ is; the atonement the priest made before the Lord is the atonement Christ is; and who has become the high priest is Jesus the Christ. The sacrifice stood in your place for your sin, and he came in the volume of the book to do the same.

precepts.text: The law having a shadow of good things to come can never with those sacrifices year by year make the comers thereunto perfect; that is how it was contrary to us.
precepts.point: The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.

note.label: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering

precepts.why:
This is how the law of sacrifice was contrary to us: “the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us. The Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for He had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice.

If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.

precepts.text: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as ye see the day approaching.
precepts.point: Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin, and there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment; that is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
Israel is referred to as a camp all through these chapters: the leper, the one with an issue and the one defiled by the dead were put out “without the camp”, “that they defile not their camps, in the midst whereof I dwell.” The Lord is gathering his camp back together again to come and deliver us; if you are not in a camp, get in a camp.

“And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.”

Inside the camp we consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works; the stronger in faith exhort the weaker to keep striving and endure to the end. If you are not gathered you cannot do that, and you do a disservice to the Lord and to your people, and so much the more as we see the day approaching.

precepts.text: Sinning willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth leaves no more sacrifice for sins, only judgment; the despiser of the covenant is counted worthy of sorer punishment.
precepts.point: Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin, and there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment; that is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin. “For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.”

“He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?”

The despiser of the covenant is counted worthy of sorer punishment than the one who died under Moses’ law. Forsaking the camp after the truth is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days; there is no more sacrifice for it, only a fearful looking for of judgment.

precepts.point: There is also no tabernacle today to do them at. The sacrifices had to be done at the tabernacle, and Israel is scattered everywhere in captivity, not able to go to Jerusalem to a temple that is not standing.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
The dedication of the altar is summed up: twelve chargers of silver, twelve silver bowls, twelve spoons of gold, and all the bullocks, rams, lambs and goats for the burnt offering, the sin offering and the peace offerings. Israel does not do the animal sacrifices anymore.

“Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.” The Most High had no pleasure in them, because the people’s minds were not changed when they offered them.

“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” Christ was the ultimate sacrifice: “He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” The sacrifices offered by the law are the first; Christ took them away to establish the second.

There is also no tabernacle today to do them at. The sacrifices had to be done at the tabernacle, and Israel is scattered everywhere in captivity, not able to go to Jerusalem to a temple that is not standing.

precepts.text: He taketh away the first covenant of sacrifices to establish the second; we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all, while the priests stood daily offering sacrifices which can never take away sins.
precepts.point: He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second: Christ offered his body once for all, where the priests stood daily offering the same sacrifices which can never take away sins. Thank the Most High for Jesus Christ, because these ordinances cannot be fulfilled in captivity.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

precepts.why:
The day of the firstfruits carried two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs, their meat and drink offerings, and a kid of the goats to make an atonement, beside the continual burnt offering. Every feast carried offerings stacked upon the daily offering, and missing them was sin.

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” The Lord said by David that He would not have the sacrifices; they could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for the people went right back to their sin.

“By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.” Christ offered his body once for all, where the priests stood daily offering the same sacrifices which can never take away sins.

Thank the Most High for Jesus Christ, because these ordinances cannot be fulfilled in captivity.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” That is where Achan fell, and unfortunately his sons and daughters and all he had with him. The Lord revealed what was hid in the earth in the midst of his tent, and the scripture cannot be broken: as Jericho was made a curse, so the one who took of it. All Israel stoned him, burned them with fire, and raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day.

Some of our people in the islands and elsewhere still ignorantly carry out such public executions to this day. We do not condone it, for we are not under the law of sacrifice now but under grace, and the judgment is of the Lord. But the fear should stay with us: Achan, an Israelite of Judah, lacked faith and was put to death, while Rahab the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for her faith. We must have the fear of the Lord in our hearts.

precepts.text: The law had a shadow of good things; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers perfect, and in them is a remembrance again made of sins every year. The Lord wants obedience over sacrifice.
precepts.point: Even in David's time he understood that sacrifice and offering were not what the Lord desired. There are multiple places where the Lord was not looking for the sacrifices.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” If they could, “would they not have ceased to be offered?” Instead, “in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.” The sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers perfect; they only brought the sins back to mind each year. The Lord wants obedience over sacrifice, which is why David says “burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.”

Sacrifice is just a show of your obedience. The Pharisees liked to say you could not get the kingdom without sacrifice, but they did not keep the commandments; they were all show and all talk, so they were the ones who could not make it to the kingdom.

precepts.text: It is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.

note.label: Psalm 50: The Mighty God Judges His People and the Wicked

precepts.why:
“For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.” That is why the Most High asks Israel, “Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?” Those sacrifices never took away sin. This is why Christ had to die: the blood of bulls and goats could not do it.

Psalm 50 was already pointing past the sacrifices to mercy, thanksgiving and paying vows to the most High. He will have mercy and not sacrifice, because sacrifice could never take the sin away, and Christ's death is what does.

precepts.text: Sacrifice, offerings, and burnt offerings the Most High would not; he desires obedience.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law”. Sacrifice, offerings and burnt offerings the Most High would not; he had no pleasure in them. He desires obedience.

This is the same thing David said: “thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” Samuel said to obey is better than sacrifice, and Ecclesiasticus says he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” Christ is written of in the volume of the book, the Old Testament.

That is what the psalm is: the stone which the builders refused becoming the head stone of the corner is written of him. He came to do the Father's will as it was written, and this is the Lord's doing, marvellous in our eyes.

precepts.text: The one offering of Christ's body that takes away sin and fulfills the sacrifices of the law ties in exactly with this chapter.

note.label: Isaiah 53: The Suffering Servant Bears Our Sins

precepts.why:
This whole chapter is the sacrifice that Christ made, why he made it, what he went through, and the fact that he bore our sins. Hebrews 10 ties in exactly. “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” “For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.” In those sacrifices “there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.”

So “when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”. “Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” That prepared body is the one brought “as a lamb to the slaughter”, that “made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth.” It pleased the Lord to bruise him and make “his soul an offering for sin”.

“He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.” The one offering of Christ’s body takes away sin and fulfils the sacrifices of the law that could never take it away. He “bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors”, and “by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.”

precepts.text: If we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins.
precepts.point: The distinction is between what falls out and what is planned. A sheep does not fall into a pit by appointment, and spilt milk is cleaned up when it happens. Wilful sin is the thing thought out beforehand.

note.label: Matthew 12: Lord of the Sabbath and the Blasphemy Against the Holy Ghost

precepts.why:
They set a man with a withered hand before him and asked, “Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.” His answer: a man with one sheep that falls into a pit on the sabbath day, “will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.”

The distinction is between what falls out and what is planned. A sheep does not fall into a pit by appointment, and spilt milk is cleaned up when it happens. What is condemned is the wilful thing, the thing thought out beforehand: “For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins”. Wilful sin, after the knowledge of the truth has been received, is the sin with no more sacrifice for it.

Lifting a sheep out of a pit, or healing a man whose hand was withered, is doing well when the need falls out on the sabbath; it is not a wilful breaking of it, and it is lawful.

precepts.text: If we sin wilfully there remains no more sacrifice; he that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses, and sorer punishment awaits those who tread under foot the Son of God, for it is fearful to fall into the hands of the living God.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.”

Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully. “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God”. The punishment under Christ is sorer, not lighter.

There is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure. “Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” Ananias fell into those hands.

“Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. When Christ came, sacrifice and offerings were no longer in effect, because Christ would be the ultimate sacrifice. We were not justified by the sacrificial law, but by Christ.

precepts.why:
Some people are only here for what benefit they can suck out of this truth, and it is never a righteous thing they are looking for. “For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry.” Paul is reminding the Israelites, the Hebrews: he will not wait long. “Now the just shall live by faith:” You brothers and sisters, the just, those of you that are in here sincerely in this truth, live by faith. “but if any man draw back,” If any of you draw back, you decide, you know what, I'm going back out into the world, or I'm going to separate and do my own thing and curse the brothers and sisters that taught me: that is drawing back; you are not in the truth. “my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” You ever notice the spirits that draw back all of a sudden get revelations of great wisdom? I drew back from you all, I don't believe what you all believe, but God has now endowed me with wisdom: this is when the days begin, this is when the Sabbath begins. It is a pattern; it is the same thing from decades past, so it is no shock any more. It is like the same demon that jumps on people and says, now you have the wisdom, go ahead and do your thing: the days are wrong, and I have the wisdom and you don't. It is the same spirit. And they all say they are not drawing back, they are still in the truth, with all the evil. The scripture says if you have hatred in your heart for your brother you are a murderer, and no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. So you call the police on a brother, get him locked up unlawfully, get his furniture taken, his kids sleeping on the floor, even try to get his kids thrown out, then get on YouTube and Facebook and say I'm still in the truth? What scripture allows that? The god they are following is called Beelzebub, Satan, Lord of the Flies. But they are still in the truth.

“But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition;” We are not of them who draw back unto hell; that is what perdition means, hell. You leave this truth, you have drawn back unto hell. “but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.” That is what we are: we believe unto the saving of the soul.
